title: cfg detection false negatives and missing is_test backfill mute blocking rules
description:
Two high-severity holes in c483406 (sutra/290, test-scope exclusion), found by Codex adversarial review and confirmed against source. Both fail in the direction of silently muting a blocking rule.

1. `#[cfg_attr(test, ...)]` misclassified as test-only. `attribute_marks_test` (src/parser/rust.rs) strips the `cfg` prefix and looks for a bare `test` token, so `cfg_attr(test, derive(PartialEq))` on a production item matches. The item's whole line range is then skipped by patterns.rs and its imports flagged is_test=1, so production code bypasses blocking forbidden_pattern / forbidden_dep / no_cycles. Same class: the `not(` bail is a literal substring check, so `#[cfg(not (test))]` (whitespace before the paren) also falls through to bare-token matching and classifies as test.

2. Existing indexes never backfill is_test. migrations/0053_import_is_test.sql adds the column with DEFAULT 0, but is_test is only written at parse time, and pipeline.rs:208-214 skips reparse when content_hash is unchanged. An upgraded workspace keeps every pre-migration cfg(test) import marked production indefinitely, with nothing in constraint evaluation detecting it. sutra/290 AC4 holds on a fresh index and can read false on any pre-existing one.

acceptance_criteria.text: cfg predicate is matched structurally, not by substring: cfg_attr(test, ...) is treated as production
cfg(not(test)) and cfg(not (test)) both stay production regardless of whitespace
Regression tests cover cfg_attr(test, ...), spaced not-predicates, and cfg(all(test, ...)) / cfg(any(test, ...)) still classifying as test
Upgrading a pre-0053 index repopulates is_test on Rust files without requiring a manual reindex
Test covers the upgrade path from a pre-0053 DB containing cfg(test) imports

execution_record: Fixed as planned. `cfg_predicate_is_test` evaluates predicates against a single soundness question — does this hold only in a test build — which also corrected `any(test, ..)`: the prior code treated it as test scope, but a sibling operand can hold in release, so it is production. That is a deliberate behaviour change beyond the reported bug, and the acceptance criterion as originally filed (asserting any(test,..) stays test scope) was wrong; docs in both repos updated to match. Backfill went in as migration 0054 rather than editing 0053, because applied migrations are content-hash pinned and 0053 was already applied locally. Verified: cargo test 1484 passed, cargo clippy --lib clean on the touched file (re-checked with indexing_slicing re-enabled, since an unrelated working-tree edit had commented that lint out). Doc half landed in vidhi 84537e3.
root_cause: Both defects came from reading Rust attributes as text rather than structure, and from assuming a schema migration is enough to change parse-derived data. `attribute_marks_test` matched a "cfg" prefix plus a bare `test` token anywhere after it, which `cfg_attr(test, ..)` and `cfg(not (test))` (whitespace defeating the literal `not(` guard) both satisfy. Separately, `imports.is_test` is only written during parsing, and the pipeline short-circuits on an unchanged content_hash, so migration 0053 adding the column with DEFAULT 0 left pre-existing indexes permanently wrong with nothing to detect it.

messages.author: codex
messages.text: Codex adversarial review of c483406..77b48f8: no findings against this task. The structural cfg predicate parser (src/parser/rust.rs) and the 0054 content_hash-clearing backfill migration survived an attack pass targeting cfg_attr nesting, spaced not-predicates, all/any combinators, migration idempotency, and the pipeline.rs reparse-skip path. Overall verdict needs-attention; findings are on sutra/292 (escape hatch missing from dep/cycle paths) and sutra/294 (external first-match shadowing include_tests).
